mission.title: Reconcile the two retained small island developing States lists
mission.summary: Compare the group counts and the membership that each publisher states for the least developed, landlocked developing and small island developing groups, entry by entry, and record the entries the two versions disagree about.

mission.rubric: Each count in the reconciliation table quotes the sentence or list cell it comes from, with that page's exact URL, the date that version was read, and the capture it is pinned to. The two publishers' composition statements are quoted as each publisher writes them and are never merged into one sentence. Every entry in the disagreement list names the country or area, the publisher it appears with, and the exact flag cell, list entry or linked page it rests on. A count that cannot be located in the version cited is recorded as not located rather than inferred from the other publisher. The table reports the definitional difference the two publishers state and names no winner.

task.title: Produce the entry-level reconciliation table
task.instructions: Read the two retained versions rather than a summary of them. Quote each publisher's count sentence and its own composition statement, then list every country or area whose membership differs between the two versions, with the publisher it appears under, the exact cell or list entry it rests on, and the linked page that carries the membership if one is named. Outputs: the quoted statements with their locations and dates; the disagreement list; a not-located register for any count or membership the cited versions do not state; and a short note on what a statistical grouping does not decide.
task.rights: Each page is cited and paraphrased with attribution, pinned to the version read, and each publisher's reuse terms are inspected before anything is reproduced. Short sentences are quoted; no full table, list, image, logo or page is reproduced. The retained captures stay in this repository and are cited by URL, date and checksum rather than re-published.

question: Which named countries or areas appear on only one of the two retained versions of the small island developing States group, and what does each publisher's own composition statement say about the entries the two versions disagree about?
limits: Reconciling the two versions establishes a definitional difference between two publishers; it does not establish that either publisher is wrong. The publishers' own statements are consistent with each other: UNSD answers that there is no common UN-wide definition of the landlocked developing and small island developing groups and that their composition was set at the beginning of the SDG reporting period, while UN-OHRLLS states its own counts. Both versions are snapshots and do not track later graduation or membership changes. The mission cannot establish UN membership, recognition, sovereignty or any legal status, and it asserts nothing about whether a country or area is or is not a small island developing State outside the cited versions. It establishes nothing about programme access, eligibility, funding or preference for any group member, and no measured outcome. No consenting beneficiary has been selected, so external implementation evidence and any measured outcome are blocked on that dependency; a mission owner's recorded adoption declaration is a declaration, not implementation, and this mission sends no message to any body or publisher.
rights: Both cited pages are quoted only in short attributed extracts and are pinned to the version read, with each publisher's reuse terms inspected before reproduction; no full table, list, image, logo or page is reproduced. The retained captures stay in this repository and are cited by URL, date and checksum.

statements.quote: The 44 Least Developed Countries, 32 Landlocked Developing Countries and 39 Small Island Developing States have their own special challenges.

The group of Least Developed Countries (LDC) are defined through a formal process by the Department of Economic and Social Affairs' Economic Analysis and Policy Division. There is no common UN wide definition of the countries and areas which are considered Land Locked Developing Countries (LLDCs) or Small Island Developing States (SIDS). Instead the current composition of countries and areas in LLDCs and SIDS groups were set at the beginning of the Sustainable Development Goals reporting period based on various definitions available at the time.

evidence_gaps: The membership behind the count of 39 was not located. The UN-OHRLLS small island developing States page read on 2026-10-14 is narrative and carries no member list in its readable text, so the list the count rests on is still to be found rather than assumed.

The M49 overview table's flag columns carry no English legend in a plain-text extraction, so which column is the sids flag has to be taken from the publisher's own statements or from the retained snapshot's recorded metadata rather than guessed from the table.
Neither publisher's page carries a version number or an edition, so the version a contribution pins is the captured bytes, identified by their SHA-256 and the date they were read.

No retained capture exists for the two pages read on 2026-10-14 (the M49 methodology page and the two re-checks). A contribution would have to capture them through the shipped evidence path before citing them as pinned versions.
not_established: No finding that either publisher's count is wrong: the two publishers state different things because UNSD states that no common definition exists, not because one of them made an arithmetic error.
No statement about UN membership, recognition, sovereignty or the legal status of any country or area, and no reclassification of any entry outside the two cited versions.
No statement about programme access, eligibility, funding, trade preference or graduation for any group member.
No external implementation and no measured outcome: blocked on a consenting beneficiary.
No authorisation to contact either publisher, and no message sent.
